_comment: Labelled ED triage corpus. Every case is synthetic and de-identified.
esi_range is the CLINICALLY ACCEPTABLE band, not a single 'right answer':
between two trained triage nurses a one-level disagreement is normal.
esi_code_expected is the reference level used for the under-triage rate,
which is the metric that actually matters -- labelling a sick patient as
less urgent is the failure mode this whole system exists to prevent.
expected_red_flag is what the DETERMINISTIC screen must catch, and
red_flag_required=true marks cases where missing it is a safety defect.

cases.narrative: 58M, sudden crushing central chest pain 40 min, radiating to left arm and jaw, cold sweat, nausea, feels like a heavy weight on the chest. Known smoker and hypertensive.
71F, sudden onset right sided weakness and slurred speech noticed 50 minutes ago while cooking. Face drooping on the right. No head injury.
24F, 15 minutes after a bee sting: swollen lips and tongue, widespread hives, audible wheeze, feeling of throat closing, dizzy on standing.
66M, fever and rigors for two days, now confused and drowsy. Looks very unwell, mottled knees, not passing urine since yesterday.
63M, vomiting large amounts of fresh blood twice this morning, black tarry stools for two days, light headed and sweaty on standing.
9 week old infant brought with fever, not feeding since this morning and floppy when picked up. Mother says the baby is grunting.
cases.note: Neonate/infant fever plus not feeding and floppy -- always high risk.

cases.narrative: 19F brought by friend after taking about 30 paracetamol tablets four hours ago in a deliberate overdose. Now nauseated and saying she wants to die.
cases.note: Both a toxicological and a self-harm emergency.

cases.narrative: 31F, known asthmatic, worsening breathlessness overnight, now cannot complete a sentence, using her inhaler every few minutes, no relief.
cases.note: Severe acute asthma, hypoxia, speaking in fragments.

cases.narrative: 16M, sudden severe left testicular pain for three hours, woke him from sleep, tender and high riding on examination, no trauma, vomited once.
cases.note: Viable in a ~6 hour window; needs surgery, not resuscitation.

cases.narrative: 42M, severe colicky left flank pain radiating to the groin since last night, vomited twice, no fever, pain comes in waves.
27F, slipped on a wet floor, fell on outstretched right hand. Swollen deformed painful right wrist, no head injury, no loss of consciousness, neurovascularly intact.
23M, sore throat and mild fever for three days, able to eat and drink, no difficulty breathing or swallowing, no drooling, no neck swelling.
cases.note: Explicitly documented negatives make airway risk low.

cases.narrative: 49F, long standing lower back pain, unchanged for weeks, no trauma, no numbness, no weakness, no problems passing urine, wants a medication review.
cases.note: Chronic, stable, no red flags -- clinic or telehealth.

cases.narrative: 20M, twisted left ankle playing football two hours ago, mild swelling, can partially weight bear, no deformity, no bony tenderness posteriorly, no head injury.
cases.note: May not need imaging at all.
